name: finalizing work in git
from: Finished work sitting in the working tree, indistinguishable from work in flight: nothing marks what settled, no history records when it settled, and closing a session loses the boundary between done and not.
to: The settled work is a commit — staged deliberately, no more and no less than what settled, described by a message naming what was finalized and by what act, and pushed wherever the firm's copies live — so the repository history carries the boundary between finished and in-flight.
cost: Attention at every close of work: reading the tree's actual state, staging exactly the settled files, writing the message, and refusing to sweep unfinished work in alongside.
otherwise: Work finalizes by accident — whenever someone happens to commit — so the history records sessions rather than settlements, and nobody can read back what was finished, when, or by whose act.

x-provenance.derived-from: user instruction of 2026-07-16 — doing git stuff is a duty, and it belongs to the office of the folk who finalize work
